name: number vertices by breadth-first levels from a peripheral start
mechanism: start at a vertex of low degree far from the centre, visit the graph level by level breadth-first (neighbours in increasing degree), and number the vertices in visiting order (reversing the order at the end); connected vertices then have nearby numbers so the matrix nonzeros hug the diagonal

sources.ref: List of algorithms (revid 1373672109), entry 'Cuthill–McKee algorithm' in section Computational mathematics / Numerical algorithms / Linear algebra: reduce the bandwidth of a symmetric sparse matrix

fails_when: a bad starting vertex gives a wide band
